classification.difficultyReason: This is the same two-elevation, perpendicular-direction structure as p14-q1, but the triangle scaffolds are removed. The student must complete the partly supplied diagram and see that north and west give a right angle at the pole's foot. They then find two ground distances with tan and combine them by Pythagoras. The right angle is stated through the compass directions rather than needing bearing reasoning. There is no show-that step or separate elevation sub-question as in p15-q5, so the demand sits just above p14-q1 and below p15-q5.

content.prompt: From a point $A$ due north of a flagpole $80\text{ m}$ tall on level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the flagpole is $38^\circ$. From a point $B$ due west of the flagpole, the angle of elevation of the top of the flagpole is $47^\circ$. Complete the diagram and calculate the distance $AB$ to the nearest metre.

spec.description: Retains the incomplete diagram: no A-to-top sight line, height or elevation labels. A simple outline flag replaces decorative flag artwork. Ordinary geometry is black.
spec.mathematics: OA and OB are perpendicular ground segments; AB is labelled d; the pole is vertical and the B-to-top sight line is dashed.
spec.answerVisibility: Missing line and numerical annotations remain absent for students to complete.

answer.short: $AB\approx127\text{ m}$, with the completed diagram shown.
answer.worked:
$OA\perp OB$ because north and west are perpendicular directions.
$$\begin{aligned}OA&=\frac{80}{\tan38^\circ}\\OB&=\frac{80}{\tan47^\circ}\\AB^2&=OA^2+OB^2\\AB&=\sqrt{\left(\frac{80}{\tan38^\circ}\right)^2+\left(\frac{80}{\tan47^\circ}\right)^2}\\AB&\approx127\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Complete self-contained answer figure adds the missing sight line, height and elevation labels.
spec.mathematics: Height 80 m; angle at A 38 degrees; angle at B 47 degrees; OA perpendicular to OB.
